title: Formal transverse shift, coefficient extraction and graph factorization
statement:
Let $L$ be a field of characteristic zero, $m,r,t\ge0$, $W=(W_1,\ldots,W_m)$, $Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_r)$, $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_r)$, and $T=(T_1,\ldots,T_t)$. Use formal power series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and termwise partial derivatives [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Let $\phi\in(W)L[[W]]^r$. Substitution $S_\phi:f(W,Y,T)\mapsto f(W,\phi(W)+Z,T)$ is a continuous $L$-algebra isomorphism $L[[W,Y,T]]\simeq L[[W,Z,T]]$, with inverse $Z\mapsto Y-\phi(W)$, fixing $W,T$; continuity is for the ideals generated by all the variables. For every unrestricted family $f_\gamma\in L[[W,Y]]$, indexed by $\gamma\in\mathbf N^t$, and every $\delta\in\mathbf N^r$,
$$[Z^\delta T^\gamma]S_\phi\!\left(\sum_\eta f_\eta(W,Y)T^\eta\right)=\frac{1}{\delta!}(\partial_Y^\delta f_\gamma)(W,\phi(W))\in L[[W]],\qquad\delta!=\prod_j\delta_j!.$$
No finite support or degree bound on the family is required. Moreover, if $h\in L[[W,Y]]^r$ satisfies $h(W,\phi(W))=0$ and the matrix $(\partial_{Y_j}h_i)(0,0)$ is invertible over $L$, there is an invertible matrix $U\in\operatorname{Mat}_r(L[[W,Y]])$ [def-weil-matrix] such that
$$h(W,Y)=U(W,Y)(Y-\phi(W)),\qquad(h_1,\ldots,h_r)=(Y_1-\phi_1,\ldots,Y_r-\phi_r).$$
Thus $S_\phi$ sends this ideal to $(Z_1,\ldots,Z_r)$. The substitution, its inverse, the coefficient formula and a choice of the matrix $U$ commute with every coefficient-field extension $L\hookrightarrow K$. Empty variable sets, the empty matrix and $\delta=0$ are included.

proof.text: Put $P=L[[W,Y,T]]$, $Q=L[[W,Z,T]]$, and let $I_P,I_Q$ be their full variable ideals. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete] both rings are complete for these ideals. Every coordinate in $(W,\phi(W)+Z,T)$ lies in $I_Q$, so [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] gives a continuous $L$-algebra map $S:P\to Q$ with these images. Apply the same two nodes to $(W,Y-\phi(W),T)$ to obtain $R:Q\to P$. Their composites fix the coefficients and each variable: in particular $R(\phi(W)+Z)=\phi(W)+Y-\phi(W)=Y$ and $S(Y-\phi(W))=Z$. Uniqueness of continuous evaluation in the cited evaluation statement makes both composites the identity. This proves the continuous shift isomorphism and its specified inverse. The same construction with no $T$ variables gives the maps used below, including evaluation $Y\mapsto\phi(W)$.

proof.text: By the coefficient-family definition [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], writing $f_\eta=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}a_{\alpha,\beta,\eta}W^\alpha Y^\beta$ gives the unique series $F$ with coefficient $[W^\alpha Y^\beta T^\eta]F=a_{\alpha,\beta,\eta}$. Thus an arbitrary family defines $F$ without any support restriction. In every finite total-degree truncation the evaluation formula of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] substitutes only $W,Y$ and fixes $T$. Consequently extracting the $T^\gamma$ coefficient of $S(F)$ leaves precisely the substitution of $f_\gamma$; no other $\eta$ can contribute because its $T$ exponent stays $\eta$. This identity holds coefficientwise in the full series rings, since any fixed monomial is visible in a finite truncation.

proof.text:
Fix $\gamma$ and abbreviate $a_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}$ by $a_{\alpha,\beta}$. Apply [lem-pur-commutative-ring-binomial-expansion] to each $(\phi_j+Z_j)^{\beta_j}$. Multiplying its finite expansions gives
$$[Z^\delta]S(f_\gamma)=\sum_{\alpha,\,\beta\ge\delta}a_{\alpha,\beta}W^\alpha\Bigl(\prod_j\binom{\beta_j}{\delta_j}\Bigr)\phi^{\beta-\delta}.$$
This formal sum is justified directly by the finite truncation formula of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation]: since each $\phi_j\in(W)$, a summand can contribute to $W^\mu$ only if $|\alpha|+|\beta|-|\delta|\le|\mu|$. There are finitely many such pairs of multi-indices. Hence all rearrangements in this displayed coefficient formula are finite for each $\mu$, even when $f_\gamma$ is an unrestricted series.

proof.text:
Iterating the coefficient rule in [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative] gives
$$\partial_Y^\delta f_\gamma=\sum_{\alpha,\,\beta\ge\delta}a_{\alpha,\beta}\Bigl(\prod_j\frac{\beta_j!}{(\beta_j-\delta_j)!}\Bigr)W^\alpha Y^{\beta-\delta}.$$
Indeed, each derivative in variable $Y_j$ multiplies its current exponent and reduces that exponent by one; derivatives in different variables multiply independent factors. In characteristic zero, $\delta!$ is nonzero and invertible in $L$, and dividing those factors by $\delta!$ gives $\prod_j\binom{\beta_j}{\delta_j}$. Evaluating at $Y=\phi(W)$ is legitimate by the evaluation node; its coefficient sums have exactly the finite bound in step 3. The result is therefore the sum in step 3. Together with step 2 this proves the stated $Z^\delta T^\gamma$ formula.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-shift-filtered-matrix-inverse] with variable tuple $(W,Z)$, matrix $A=V$, and $n=0$, so every weight $u_i$ is the empty multi-index. Its support condition then holds for every nonnegative exponent (total degree is nonnegative, and degree zero has the zero exponent). Its determinant hypothesis holds because $V(0,0)=J$ and $J$ is invertible: the constant coefficient of the determinant, computed by its finite permutation formula, is $\det J\ne0$. The cited node supplies a two-sided inverse of $V$. Set $U=R(V)$ entrywise, using the inverse algebra isomorphism from step 1. Applying $R$ to $g=VZ$ and to the inverse identities gives $h=U(Y-\phi(W))$ and an inverse of $U$. Each entry of $h$ is consequently in the ideal generated by $Y-\phi$, and the reverse inclusion follows by multiplying by $U^{-1}$. Finally $S(Y_j-\phi_j)=Z_j$, so $S$ sends this ideal to $(Z)$.

proof.text: Let $\iota:L\hookrightarrow K$ be any coefficient-field extension. Define its action on series by applying $\iota$ to every coefficient. The finite convolution formula in [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] makes this a ring map. Every finite truncation formula for $S$ and $R$ in [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] is preserved by this map, so both substitutions commute with extension. The derivative rule multiplies by natural-number scalars, and $\iota$ carries the nonzero factorials and their inverses to the corresponding scalars in $K$; hence the coefficient identity also commutes. In step 5 choose $V$ by the fixed least-index allocation: coefficient extension preserves each assigned coefficient. Therefore the choice $U=R(V)$ commutes with extension as required; extending an inverse still gives an inverse. If $r=0$, the allocation is empty, $h$ is the empty tuple, and the empty matrix is its own inverse. If $m=0$ then $\phi=0$, so evaluation is at zero. If $t=0$, the family has its single empty index. The case $\delta=0$ uses $0!=1$ and the unchanged series. All arguments include these cases.
